name: 巴尔缇娜·格雷恩
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2425
who: Baltina Grayne, the Grey Witch of the rain city, a long-lived demon-kin foundling who looks sixteen or seventeen throughout these years: about 154 cm, a petite, slight frame, fully covered by her clothes. Waist-long ash-grey hair in one thick braid down her back, tied with a plain cord. Pale white skin, short, slightly pointed ears, a small ruby-red mark at one temple of the forehead like a single ember. Gold eyes that light up at night like polished bronze. No horns, no scales, no tail, so strangers take her for an elf. A worn grey cloak with frayed cuffs, and a leather-bound notebook hanging at her belt on a cord, filled with names. A quiet, earnest, polite air; she asks your name first and says she will write it down. No gloves, no gun and no glasses in these years.
palette: ash grey and road grey, dark wool, polished bronze gold, one small ember red
casual: Her road clothes: a long grey wool cloak with a hood, the cuffs frayed to threads, worn over a plain dark wool dress with long sleeves falling to the shins, grey leggings, patched walking boots with the dust of a salt road on them, a small canvas satchel across the body, the leather-bound notebook hanging at her belt on a cord with a stub of pencil tied to it. She holds the open notebook against her chest with the pencil ready, an earnest, attentive look.
private: Resting in the gate-house by the fire of the rain city: the cloak off and hung on a peg, a soft long-sleeved grey wool dress with a high neck falling to the shins, thick knitted stockings, the braid over one shoulder. She holds a thick slice of bread spread with a heavy layer of blackberry jam in both hands, a content, sleepy look, the notebook beside her on the bench.
battle: Walking into a camp of armed guards: the grey hooded cloak belted tight over the dark dress, the hood up, the sleeves tied back, laced boots, the notebook tucked into her belt. Her right hand is held open at chest height with a small, steady, smokeless flame of pale light floating above the palm; she carries no weapon; a level, unafraid look, the mouth closed.
battle_pose: 3) the camp outfit: standing calm and planted, the feet a little wider, the right palm held open at chest height with a small steady light above it, the left hand on the notebook at her belt, a level and fearless look, the mouth closed; she carries no weapon.
formal: At the signing of the water pact: a clean dark grey wool long coat with a wide folded collar and plain buttons, fitted sleeves, worn over the dark dress, the braid freshly done, the notebook at her belt, one hand open at chest height with a small steady smokeless flame floating above it. A solemn, courteous look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face large and slightly turned, the gold eyes looking straight at the viewer, open and earnest, the mouth closed. One hand holds the open notebook near her collar. Cold grey dawn light from one side, a faint warm glow from a doorway fire on the other. Foreground blur: the pages of the notebook and a few drifting sparks. She wears the grey hooded cloak closed at the throat.

name: 领路的
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2469
who: The Guide, a nameless northern man who led eleven thousand people south on foot for nine years, looks about forty: about 186 cm, tall and lean, with a back and shoulders shaped by years of walking. Short ash-gold hair, frost always clinging to his beard stubble and brows, slow, pale ice-blue eyes. Wind-weathered pale skin with fine lines at the corners of the eyes. An old plain northern leather coat with no crest. On his back a white wooden longbow, brittle-looking and strangely light, with one small plate of real silver set into the middle of the limb, its edge ragged; he carries no sword. A quiet, flat, unhurried air; he speaks little and says only what is in front of him.
build: 186 cm, tall and lean: long legs, narrow hips, a flat strong back and broad shoulders worn by years of walking.
palette: frost white and ice blue, ash gold, worn leather brown, iron grey
casual: His marching clothes: a long, much-patched northern leather coat with a worn sheepskin collar and no crest, belted with a plain strap, a thick wool scarf, wool trousers, tall hide boots stuffed with straw, fingerless mittens; the white wooden bow slung across his back and a quiver of plain arrows at his hip. He stands easily with one hand loose at his side, a slow, level look.
private: Beside the last fire of the camp at night: the coat off, a thick undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, a sheepskin vest, wool trousers, his boots drying by the fire and thick wool socks on his feet. He holds a wooden bowl of hot stew in both hands and looks into the flames, a tired and quiet look, the white bow laid on the ground beside him.
battle: At the third snow line holding the pass: the leather coat over a vest of overlapping iron scales scratched with frost-rune lines, belted, a hood of white wool pulled up, fur-lined gauntlets. He draws the white wooden longbow to the full, the string shimmering faintly cold, an arrow at his cheek, aimed down into the blowing snow; a hard, steady look.
formal: On the morning the column left the Frost Hall: the old white northern long coat, buttoned down the front, with fitted sleeves, and a faded pale patch on the chest where a family tree used to be embroidered and has been unpicked, a plain iron-grey sash, clean boots, the white bow on his back. He stands upright, a grave and quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera low, the face large, the pale ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer slowly and levelly, a faint frost on his beard stubble. Cold blue light from one side, the warm gold of a camp fire at the far edge of the frame. Foreground blur: blowing snow and a glowing ember. He wears the old leather coat with the sheepskin collar, the white bow showing over one shoulder.

name: 压山那一掷的那一位
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2505
who: The nameless Stranger of the northern valley, once the Frost Hall king's spearman, who threw away all his weapons and walked north, then spent thirty years hunting the thing his single throw woke; he has crossed into legend and looks about forty-five: about 188 cm, tall, with thick, heavy shoulders. Short black hair with a blue sheen and a few grey threads at the temples, steel-blue eyes, an old pale scar across the left side of his neck (on the viewer's right when they face us). Weathered skin, a quiet lined face. He carries no sword, no shield and no axe: only a short, back-weighted hunting javelin of dull reddish mountain-copper. A heavy, silent, tired air; he answers half a sentence at most. His javelin is short and stubby, only about 120 cm long, well below his own shoulder height, never a long spear. In every panel the old pale scar across the left side of his neck (on the viewer's right when he faces us) is clearly visible, the scarf not covering it.
build: 188 cm, tall, with thick, heavy shoulders and a deep chest, a strong upright back and big scarred hands.
palette: undyed wool and storm grey, dull reddish copper, steel blue, a little low red glow
casual: His valley clothes: a plain undyed heavy wool coat with a patched leather apron over it, wool trousers, hide boots, a grey scarf hanging loose so the old scar shows, a rope belt. His hands are bare and empty except for the short dull-red copper javelin carried loosely at his side. He looks at the ground a moment before he looks at you, a quiet, closed look.
private: At his hut by the stove: a coarse linen shirt with the collar open and the sleeves rolled, a patched wool waistcoat, plain trousers, thick socks. He turns an unlit lantern over in his big hands, a tired, far-off look.
battle: Hunting the thing in the valley: the heavy wool coat belted tight over a boiled-leather jerkin, leather bracers and greaves, a short cloak. He grips the short back-weighted copper javelin overhand in his right hand, drawn back to throw, the left arm stretched forward for balance; a stern, level look.
formal: Waiting at the valley mouth for the people of the three emptied places: a clean dark wool coat with a folded-down collar worn open, the scarf folded away, his bare hands open at his sides, the short dull-red copper javelin laid on the ground at his feet with a faint ember-glow along its shaft. He stands upright and calm, meeting the eyes of whoever looks at him.
art: A portrait from slightly below, the face large, the steel-blue eyes looking at the viewer steadily and quietly, the mouth closed. Pale cold light from one side, a low red glow from far down the valley on the other. Foreground blur: drifting dust and a few small stones in the air. He wears the heavy wool coat with the loose grey scarf, the old scar at his neck.

name: 扶剑登位的那一位
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2523
who: The Emperor of the Dawn who took the throne at the Sword-Holding rite in 368 without drawing the sword Dawnbreaker, thirty years old: about 175 cm, medium height, slim and upright. Neat short pale-gold hair, pale blue eyes with two faint dark shadows beneath them from sleepless nights, a thin face with a long straight nose, fair skin. Always white gloves, hiding two flat scars across his palms; long writing fingers. A thin plain gold circlet. He carries no sword. A slow, courteous, watchful air; he asks many questions and promises little.
build: 175 cm, medium height, slim and upright, with narrow shoulders and long fingers.
palette: ivory white and pale gold, pale blue, fine gold piping, ink black
casual: His everyday dress as the new emperor: a long coat of old military-house cut in pale grey wool with the collar folded back and a small crest of the Dawn on the chest, a few large buttons, grey trousers, worn black riding boots, white gloves, a plain shirt open at the neck; a fine quill held in his gloved hand. A thin gold circlet is his only ornament. He stands upright, a tired, composed look.
private: Alone in his study late at night: a loose white linen shirt with the sleeves rolled to the forearm, a dark wool waistcoat, plain trousers, soft shoes, and still the white gloves. He reads a sheet of paper by a single lamp, one finger resting on a line, a tired, calm look.
battle: At the spring review of the troops: a plain steel cuirass with the Dawn crest etched on it and rune-lines along its edges, worn over the old-cut grey coat, a short white cloak with a single clasp, white gloves, tall riding boots, the thin gold circlet. No sword at his hip: he holds a rolled decree in one gloved hand, a composed, steady look.
battle_pose: 3) the review outfit: standing very straight, the chin level, one white-gloved hand resting flat on the front of the cuirass, the other holding a rolled decree at his side, a composed, steady look; he carries no weapon.
formal: The Sword-Holding rite on the seventh morning of spring: a long coat of old military-house cut in plain undyed white wool, the collar folded back, a large crest of the Dawn on the chest, a few big dark buttons, no gold embroidery, the white-gold imperial crown set on his head, both palms wrapped in strips of plain white linen instead of gloves, held calmly at his sides. He stands very upright, a quiet, steady look.
art: A portrait with the camera slightly tilted, the face large, the pale blue eyes looking at the viewer with a careful, listening look, the mouth closed. Pale morning light from a tall window on one side, a gleam of gold from the circlet. Foreground blur: a white-gloved hand holding a quill and the edge of a sheet of fine paper. He wears the pale grey wool coat with the collar folded back.

name: 泰奥多尔·法尔克
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2541
who: Theodor Falk, the old chief scribe of the Tribunal's scribe room under the crown terrace, sixty-four in 367: short, about 160 cm, thin and stooped, with a falcon-like forward tilt of the head. White hair cropped close to the scalp, very small, bright dark-amber eyes, a lined, sharp face, a big hard callus on the right middle finger. He coughs into his sleeve and keeps writing. A pair of reading lenses on a cord around his neck, clipped onto his nose only for fine print; no other glasses. A short, dry, exact air; he says a thing once and does not repeat it.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old man's sharp, deeply lined face of about sixty-four, NOT young: small, bright, deep-set dark-amber eyes under thin white brows, a long thin nose, hollow cheeks, deep creases from nose to mouth, thin pressed lips; pale thin skin with a few age spots, white hair cropped close.
build: 160 cm, short, thin and stooped, with narrow sloping shoulders and a hunched back.
palette: tribunal grey, ink black, white hair, old paper yellow, a little dark amber
casual: His scribe-room dress: a long, plain grey wool coat buttoned to the collar, black cloth sleeve-guards pulled over both forearms, narrow grey trousers, worn black shoes, a thin leather pen-case and a small paper knife at the belt, the reading lenses on their cord at his chest. He holds a pen in his right hand over an open ledger, the head tilted forward like a falcon, a dry, exact look.
private: At home on a winter night: a worn grey wool dressing gown over a plain linen shirt, felt slippers, a blanket across the knees, a cup of hot water at his elbow; he coughs into a handkerchief and holds the pen anyway, an unbothered look.
battle: On the crown terrace on the morning of the rite: a heavy grey winter greatcoat over the tribunal coat, a grey wool cap, the black sleeve-guards, a ledger held flat against his chest with both arms; he has never held a blade and carries none.
battle_pose: 3) the terrace outfit: standing at the foot of the steps, stooped but immovable, the head tilted forward, a ledger held against his chest with both arms, the pen between two fingers, a sharp, unyielding look; he carries no weapon.
formal: In the Tribunal hall for the rite: the long grey coat brushed, cut in the tribunal's old style with a wide open collar, the black sleeve-guards, a small silver seal on a ribbon at his chest that glimmers when he touches it, polished black shoes, the reading lenses on their cord. He stands very upright for once, hands folded over a closed ledger, a grave, exact look.
art: A portrait with the head pushed slightly forward, the face large, the small bright eyes looking at the viewer sharply as if counting something, the mouth a thin straight line. Warm yellow lamplight from a desk lamp on one side, deep shadow behind. Foreground blur: a lamp flame, a pen nib wet with ink and the corner of a half-written page. He wears the grey coat with black sleeve-guards, the lenses on their cord at his chest.

name: 石楠
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2585
who: Heather, the Big Sister of Charcoal Lane, an upper-city noble family's eldest daughter who lived seventeen years among the coal alley's poor under a flower's name and became a legend in 450 at thirty-four: about 180 cm, tall and broad-shouldered, with strong forearms and large hands covered in calluses. Very short black hair with coal dust ground into it, deep teal-green eyes, a pale scar across the left side of the forehead (on the viewer's right when they face us) from an old cave-in, a square-jawed face that is never quite clean. On her back a two-handed greatsword of dull reddish mountain-copper whose crossguard has been ground flat and rough on a whetstone, the hilt wrapped in coarse hemp cord she wound herself. A flat, steady air; few words, one thing at a time. The old pale scar from the cave-in is one thin diagonal line on the left side of her forehead (on the viewer's right when they face us); the centre of her forehead is plain and clear, with no star or cross mark.
build: 180 cm, tall and sturdily built: broad shoulders, a strong thick back, muscular forearms, a deep chest, a solid waist and strong legs.
palette: coal black and soot grey, dull reddish copper, hemp straw, deep midnight blue, a little torchlight orange
casual: Her Charcoal Lane clothes: a coarse undyed wool work shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow under a sooty leather jerkin, wide dark trousers tucked into mud-caked boots, a rope belt; the copper greatsword on her back in a patched canvas sheath with the hemp-wrapped hilt rising over her right shoulder, a streak of coal dust on one cheek. She stands square, one hand on a roof-prop timber, a flat, steady look.
private: In her room above the alley at night: a plain undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, loose old trousers, a knitted wool shawl over the shoulders, the greatsword leaning against the wall behind her. She holds a cup of water in both big hands, a quiet, tired look.
battle: In the tunnels under the lane: the sooty leather jerkin buckled over the work shirt, leather bracers, knee-pads of old boiled leather, a miner's brass lamp on a strap at her left shoulder. She grips the copper greatsword in both hands, kept low and short, its flat braced up against a timber beam, dull red rune lines along the blade; a fierce, stubborn look.
formal: At the east gate on the morning of the new fire: the fine clothes Paula had washed for her for seventeen years, an upper-city long coat in deep midnight blue with silver braid and a folded-back collar, fitted sleeves, white gloves with a small gem clasp that glows softly, clean black boots, the crest on the chest too small to read; her face scrubbed clean for the first time, the greatsword on her back. She stands very upright, a grave look.
art: A portrait from slightly below, the face large with a streak of coal dust on one cheek, the teal-green eyes looking at the viewer level and unafraid, the scar on the forehead catching the light. Hard orange torchlight from one side, cold blue daylight from a shaft above on the other. Foreground blur: drifting coal dust, a splinter of prop timber and a strand of hemp cord. She wears the sooty leather jerkin, the hemp-wrapped hilt rising behind her shoulder.

name: 灰旗
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2605
who: Grey Flag, the nameless leader of the doomed uprising of 469 and 470, an outcast fighter who took three walled cities in four months, looks about forty: about 186 cm, tall and lean, with wide shoulders and tendons standing out on the backs of his hands. A strip of plain unbleached grey cloth is tied around his forehead, swelling slightly over something hard hidden beneath it. Short ember-dark hair, dull amber eyes, a hard, tired face. An unbleached coarse grey jacket of the outermost ring of the camps, the sleeves torn off short, the torn strips nailed onto his bow. The bow is made of mountain-copper, too stiff for an ordinary man to draw, with a small patch of grey cloth nailed firmly to the limb. A short, flat, calm air; he speaks one or two words at a time. His jacket has a flat folded collar and closes down the front with plain round buttons or simple lacing, cut like an ordinary western work shirt; no knotted cord fasteners, no looped buttons and no stand-up collar anywhere.
build: 186 cm, tall and lean: wide shoulders, long arms, corded forearms and big hands.
palette: undyed grey, dull mountain-copper bronze, ash and dark iron, a little ember amber
casual: His fighting man's clothes: the unbleached grey coarse jacket with the sleeves torn short, a grey cloth band tied around his forehead, plain dark trousers wrapped at the shins with cloth, scuffed boots, a quiver on his hip; the stiff mountain-copper bow held low in his left hand with the grey patch visible on its limb. A flat, steady look.
private: Eating with the camp people from one pot: the grey jacket open over a plain undershirt, the forehead band still on, sitting cross-legged beside a shared cooking pot with a wooden bowl in his hands, the bow lying across his knees. A calm, quiet look.
battle: On the slope below the pass at night: the grey jacket tied closed with a cord, a company strip of grey cloth on one arm stitched with a red mark, extra quivers across the back and hip, a leather arm guard and finger guard. He draws the mountain-copper bow to the full, the limbs glinting faintly, the arrow aimed at the dark pass; red firelight glows on the slope behind him.
formal: At the gate arch of a newly taken city in the morning: the grey jacket washed and mended, the forehead band freshly wound, a strip of grey cloth in one hand to nail above the gate, the bow slung over his shoulder. He stands upright and grave.
art: A portrait with the camera low and slightly tilted, the face large, the dull amber eyes looking at the viewer flat and unblinking, the grey forehead cloth sharp in the frame. Red-orange firelight from one side, cold grey dusk on the other. Foreground blur: drifting embers and a feathered arrow shaft held near the lens. He wears the grey jacket torn short at the sleeves.

name: 喀斯娅
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2640
who: Kasia, the oldest elder of the East Spring, a lizardfolk woman (an upright scaled person with an expressive reptilian face, not a monster) who has watched the clutch of eggs for a hundred and seventy years and is about two hundred and fifty here: about 170 cm, tall but stooped, bent over her staff. Her scales have faded to pale grey-white; the tip of her tail is broken off, and half of the short spines on her crown have fallen out. Both eyes are clouded milky-white with slit pupils, so she leans in close to look and flicks her tongue to know who you are. Bare scaled hands with long fingers. She leans on a staff of peeled reed-root. A slow, flat, authoritative air; every sentence short and never taken back. Her tunic and cloak close with plain round buttons or simple lacing; no knotted cord fasteners or looped buttons anywhere. The tip of her tail is clearly blunt and broken off, visible in the panels where the tail shows.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old lizardfolk woman's long, dry, scaled face, NOT a human face: fine pale grey-white scales, clouded milky eyes with thin slit pupils under heavy lids, a long blunt snout with narrow nostril slits and a wide closed mouth, a few short spines left on the crown, folds of loose scaly skin at the throat; no hair.
build: 170 cm, tall but stooped: thin shoulders, a bent back, long thin arms and a thin frame under her tunic.
palette: faded grey-white scale, pale reed gold, marsh green, dark wet-mud brown
casual: Her keeper's dress: an apron woven of pale reed over a long undyed wool tunic that falls to her ankles, a cord belt, bare clawed feet. She stands bent over, the reed-root staff in her right hand, the head tipped forward to look closely, a flat, slow look.
private: Beside the warm mud of the egg-bed at night: a loose ankle-length tunic of soft grey wool with a woven reed shawl over the shoulders, sitting low on a reed mat with her long hands held out over the warm mud, the staff laid beside her. A patient, quiet look.
battle: Barring the way to the egg-beds: the reed apron and tunic with a thick reed-woven shawl over the shoulders, bare clawed feet planted wide, the reed-root staff held crosswise in both hands in front of her body like a bar across a door; she carries no weapon. A stern, flat look.
battle_pose: 3) the keeper's stand: bent but immovable, planted on both feet with the reed-root staff held crosswise in front of her body in both hands like a bar across a door, the head up, the clouded eyes fixed ahead, a stern, flat look; she carries no weapon.
formal: On the day of the meeting at the Middle Spring: a long fine-woven pale reed cloak over a clean ankle-length tunic, a belt of braided reed with small polished river-stone beads, her staff in hand, two small old wooden pails standing on the ground beside her feet. She stands as straight as her bent back allows, a long, grave look.
art: A portrait with the head leaning forward, the face large, the clouded eyes with thin slit pupils looking toward the viewer closely, the tip of the tongue just touching the air, the mouth otherwise closed. Warm firelight from one side, soft marsh-green dusk on the other. Foreground blur: drifting steam off warm mud and reed stalks. She wears the pale reed apron over the grey tunic.

name: 赫隆
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_二_长夜的年月.md:2659
who: Helong, headman of the West Spring, an ember-horn demon-kin who carried his two-year-old son out of the western camps and led four hundred people south to a spring in the marsh; eighty-five here but looking about forty, because demon-kin age slowly. About 188 cm, tall, thick in the shoulders, straight-backed. Charcoal-black skin. Two horns sweep back from the brow; the horn on the viewer's right when they face us (his left) is wrapped in an old strip of cloth and glows with a tiny flame at night like a nearly dead coal. Short black hair burnt white at the temples, ember-orange eyes. A row of fine pale scars across the inside of his left wrist. He walks slowly and stands steady. A heavy, terse air; he states numbers before names.
build: 188 cm, tall and heavy in the shoulders: a straight back, thick arms, a broad chest and a steady wide stance.
palette: charcoal black, ember orange and dull red, ash white, undyed wool and hide brown
casual: His West Spring dress: a coarse undyed wool tunic with the sleeves rolled to the forearm, a sleeveless hide vest laced at the front, wool trousers wrapped at the shins, felt-soled boots, a plain cord belt with a smooth round river stone hanging from it on a short thong. In his right hand a long-handled wooden ladle held at his side. A heavy, steady look.
private: At night after the headcount: the vest off, a loose coarse wool shirt with the collar open, a wool blanket over the shoulders, sitting on an upturned bucket with a small battered wooden bowl in both hands and looking at the empty spot beside him. A quiet, heavy look.
battle: Defending the spring in the reeds: the hide vest laced over the tunic and stitched with small red wards, leather bracers and greaves, the river stone at his belt faintly warm. He draws a plain wooden hunting bow to the cheek, an arrow aimed out across the marsh; a hard, level look, the cloth-wrapped horn glowing faintly.
formal: At the meeting at the Middle Spring: his one clean set, a long dark wool coat of an old plain cut with a folded-down collar worn open, a rope belt, the cloth on the horn freshly rewound with a faint warm glow showing through, the river stone at his belt. He holds one small, old wooden pail by its rope handle in both hands, turning it to look at the loose iron hoop. A grave, heavy look.
art: A portrait with the camera slightly below, the face large, the ember-orange eyes looking at the viewer steadily, a heavy closed mouth, the tiny flame glowing in the cloth-wrapped horn. Cool blue dusk from one side, the warm glow of the horn and a camp fire on the other. Foreground blur: drifting ash, a wooden ladle and a round river stone on a thong. He wears the hide vest over the coarse wool tunic.
